attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is an unanchored-start regex `[.,;:!?)\]]+$`, which is O(k²) on a run of k punctuation characters that is not at the end of the match. A stored description with a long run of dots inside a non-space token (e.g. "https://a" followed by 100k dots and a letter) will stall every viewer's render, since tokenize runs on each render of every item page. The artifact sets no description length cap.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ... ABSENT: any max length on item.description or any bound on URL token length

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is an unanchored-start regex with a `+$` tail. On a long run of punctuation that is followed by a non-punctuation character, V8 retries from every start position and backtracks each time, so the cost is quadratic. A single owner can post a description that freezes the item page for every neighbor who views it, because nothing caps description length.
attacks.evidence: 'const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/;' applied to m[0] from URL_RE, which accepts any run of non-space characters after 'http://'. ABSENT: any maximum length on item.description or on the URL match before tokenize runs.

attacks.claim: The stated invariant is that truncation 'only cuts at whitespace or between tokens', but the fallback hard-cuts an unbroken word at the limit. The test suite asserts this mid-word cut, so the claim and the code disagree.

attacks.claim: Stripping a trailing ')' from every URL breaks URLs whose parentheses are balanced, such as Wikipedia-style paths. The link then points to a truncated, likely broken address.

attacks.claim: Length accounting mixes UTF-16 code units (.length, slice) with code points (Array.from). Emoji and other astral characters count as 2 against the 280 limit in most branches, and the fallback slice can produce a different length than the other branches.
